regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: T-DM1 links HER2 targeting to a chemotherapy payload to help control previously treated advanced breast cancer. Prior trastuzumab and a taxane, plus the full NCCP prior-treatment or early-relapse criteria, must be checked.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Previously treated HER2-positive unresectable locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: The antibody attaches to HER2. After the complex enters a cell, its DM1 payload disrupts structures needed for cell division. This is a single linked medicine, with its own dosing and safety rules.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: T-DM1 3.6 mg/kg IV every 21 days, adjusted if required, until progression or unacceptable toxicity. This metastatic course has no fixed 14-cycle endpoint; the postoperative early-breast regimen is a different card.
key_points: FBC, renal and liver profile before every cycle
Echo / MUGA every 12 weeks; around C5 for uninterrupted 21-day cycles
Agree follow-up of cardiac, liver, platelet and nerve effects at any treatment change; no universal post-T-DM1 scan calendar is assigned here.
Contact the unit to rearrange a missed dose; the next schedule preserves a 3-week interval.
Other cancer medicines need their own complete regimen rules.

Mild / moderate renal or hepatic impairment: no starting-dose adjustment in the source. Severe impairment has insufficient data; monitor carefully. Avoid strong CYP3A4 inhibitors where possible and obtain pharmacy interaction review.

Adult HER2-positive unresectable locally advanced / metastatic disease after trastuzumab and a taxane, separately or together.
Prior advanced-disease treatment OR recurrence during / within 6 months of completing adjuvant therapy; ECOG 0–2 and baseline LVEF ≥50%.
important_cautions: NCCP bilirubin Table 5 leaves >10–20 ×ULN unassigned; EMA SmPC says discontinue above 10. Encoded hold plus urgent source reconciliation, not silent normality.

premedication_and_prophylaxis: T-DM1 has low emetogenic risk; review the low-risk antiemetic draft and individual contraindications.

Surgery and radiotherapy are coordinated by the MDT. When endocrine therapy is indicated, it has its own schedule and bone-health plan.

Discuss pregnancy, fertility and contraception before treatment. Report pregnancy promptly; do not breastfeed during treatment or for 7 months afterwards. The team confirms the medicine-specific contraception duration.
special_support: Discuss fertility, practical needs, rehabilitation and psychosocial support.

baseline: Baseline cardiac assessment and LVEF are required. ECG is guided by the cardiac / clinical assessment; NCCP does not prescribe a separate fixed-cycle ECG timetable for T-DM1.
before_each_cycle: FBC, renal and liver profile before every cycle
Check symptoms and whether cardiac / imaging results are due; do not assume each test is required at every cycle.
urgent_review_signals: Call promptly for unusual bleeding, yellow eyes / skin, worsening numbness or new cough / breathlessness.

longitudinal_schedule.title: When your checks happen
longitudinal_schedule.note: Cycle examples assume no delays and count from the first dose of this schedule. If switching route or continuing previous HER2 treatment, preserve the existing echo due date. Tests are scheduled by elapsed time and clinical need; the team owns booking and result review. NCCP remains 12-weekly during treatment, including maintenance; a longer interval needs an explicit individual specialist plan.

administration.cycle_and_sequence: T-DM1 3.6 mg/kg IV every 21 days, adjusted if required, until progression or unacceptable toxicity. This metastatic course has no fixed 14-cycle endpoint; the postoperative early-breast regimen is a different card.
route_and_duration: First infusion over 90 minutes, then observe for at least 90 minutes. Later infusions may take 30 minutes if tolerated, with at least 30 minutes observation.
practical_workflow: Confirm the dose, symptoms, required blood results and echo due window.
A cannula, PICC or implanted port may be used according to the treatment plan. A port insertion is a separate procedure.
First infusion over 90 minutes, then observe for at least 90 minutes. Later infusions may take 30 minutes if tolerated, with at least 30 minutes observation.
Contact the unit to rearrange a missed dose; the next schedule preserves a 3-week interval. This medicine does not routinely require a take-home pump.
observation_and_access: The line team explains placement, dressing care and when normal activities can resume. A port is accessed with a special needle during treatment. Removal of the implanted device is a separate planned procedure when no longer needed; do not remove or adjust it yourself.

A PICC usually needs regular dressing and flushing appointments even between treatments. Fever, redness, swelling, pain, leakage or damage requires prompt advice. Your hospital supplies the exact care instructions.
